Video methods are examples, not official Catalina instructions. Verify the mast-step/tabernacle, shroud arrangement, chainplates, lifting gear and site clearance for this particular boat before following a demonstration.

On-site mast setup checklist

Review the factory manual first. The checks below are for the pre-raise briefing; do not treat the checklist as evidence of inspection.

Factory mast-stepping sequence

1 · Preparation and safety

Make the area safe, confirm the mast-raising arrangement, inspect rigging and secure loose lines. Catalina's instructions describe upper shrouds, aft lower shrouds and backstay attached before the lift.

2 · Tabernacle and pivot

Center the mast foot in the deck step, secure the pivot hardware and avoid leverage that could damage the tabernacle fittings.

3 · Controlled raise and fastening

Use coordinated crew and a positively controlled forestay line; keep personnel outside the fall area. When upright, attach the forestay and forward lower shrouds. Do not substitute an unverified gin-pole configuration.

4 · Mast alignment and tuning

Confirm fore-aft and side-to-side alignment and adjust stays per the applicable manual and hardware inspection. Do not invent rig tension numbers for unknown rigging.

Read Catalina 22 mast-stepping guidance ↗

Boom and sail sequence

1 · Set up the boom

Inspect and install the gooseneck and boom, then the vang/mainsheet and topping lift or other designed support. Confirm traveller and mainsheet attachment points match this boat.

2 · Mainsail

Identify the white mainsail by luff and fittings, inspect slides, battens and reefing equipment, feed sail into its designed track, connect tack and clew and run the main halyard without twists. Hoist only in a safe controlled setting.

3 · Headsail

Confirm whether the HOOD-branded sail is a jib or genoa; inspect hanks/furling compatibility, sheets, leads and halyard. Do not assume every sail in the photographic inventory belongs to this vessel.

4 · Final rig and function tests

Test halyards, sheets, boom movement, reefing, clearances and stowage. Use the 1977 original instructions where applicable; 1987 illustrations are secondary references.
